items.title: Put the reason before or after

states.label: Reason last
states.sm: Na alu le tama i le fale ʻona ʻua maʻi le teine.
states.en: The boy went to the house because the girl was sick.

states.label: Reason first
states.sm: ʻOna ʻua maʻi le teine, na alu ai le tama i le fale.
states.en: Because the girl was sick, the boy went to the house.
states.note: *Ai* points back to the whole reason clause.

items.caption: The because-clause keeps its own tense particle in both places. When it comes first, the other clause usually carries *ai*.

items.title: Read the particle after the joining word

states.label: A complement
states.sm: ʻUa mafai ona sau le teine.
states.note: The verb after *ona* has no tense particle: this is the that-word.

states.label: A reason
states.sm: ʻUa alu le tama ʻona ʻua sau le teine.
states.en: The boy went because the girl came.
states.note: The verb after *ʻona* carries *ʻua*: this is the because-word.

items.caption: Ordinary print often spells these joining words alike. The tense particle after them is the test; the then-construction is told apart by its closing *lea*.

items.title: A reason or a purpose?

bins.label: A purpose: what it was done for

items.sm: Sā taatia le teine i le fale ʻauā ʻua vaivai.
items.en: The girl lay down in the house because she was tired.
items.why: The because-word opens the reason under its own tense particle.

items.sm: E lē mafai ona alu le tama leaga e maʻi.
items.en: The boy cannot go because he is sick.
items.why: *Leaga* gives the unwelcome reason for the main clause.

items.sm: Sā alu le tama e ʻaumai le niu.
items.en: The boy went to bring the coconut.
items.why: The clause headed by *e* says what the going was for.

items.sm: Sā ʻou alu neʻi tagi le tama.
items.en: I went, so that the boy would not cry.
items.why: The warning particle *neʻi* makes the purpose negative: what the going was intended to prevent.

items.intro: Choose whether the added clause explains a reason or names a purpose.

items.title: A why-question and its answer

lines.sm: ʻAiseā na alu ai le tamāloa i le nuʻu?
lines.en: Why did the man go to the village?

items.caption: The printed answer needs no main clause of its own. A because-word and its reason fill the whole turn.
